title: Audience’s New Deputy Director for Coverage
body_markdown:
Jake Grovum will lead Audience editors assigned to desks across the newsroom. Read more from newsroom Audience director Anna Dubenko.


Jake Grovum, a leader on Audience who has helped shape how The Times appears on social media for the past four years, has been promoted to Audience’s deputy director for coverage. In this role, Jake will lead a growing group of Audience editors assigned to desks across the newsroom.


Jake’s team is responsible for supplying desks with actionable, strategic insights on ongoing coverage and breaking news, as well as planning effective and creative rollouts for our most ambitious journalism. In addition to conducting analysis rooted in audience data, these editors also serve as critical connection points between desks and other audience functions, like the community team, the video audience team, search, social and more.


Desk audience editors (DAEs) have already proven to be our secret weapon in uncovering and instilling audience best practices across The Times. Their effectiveness is why we now have an audience editor on nearly every desk in the newsroom. Jake’s new job will be to scale the impact of this group and partner with newsroom leaders to uncover more audience opportunities.


Additionally, Jake will be responsible for the team’s regular audience reporting for daily news meetings, and the audience insights about our coverage that we bring to newsroom leadership in other venues.


“This is a moment when we need more than ever to understand how best to serve our global audience. In other words, it is a moment for Jake,” said Michael Slackman. “He has long been a terrific partner in helping to guide the newsroom and quick to offer smart insights paired with actionable suggestions. We are very lucky to have him take on this leadership role.”


He will also be the Audience team’s partner to editors for investigations and major enterprise, working closely with Jim Yardley and his team to grow an engaged audience for signature Times journalism.


People who have worked for or with Jake will tell you that he’s an empathetic leader who will jump in during a busy news cycle and work shoulder-to-shoulder with his team. He’s also adept at zooming out and connecting the dots between the newsroom’s needs in a shifting digital landscape. He’s also an accomplished tie-dyer.


Jake came to The Times in 2019 from The Financial Times, where he worked as a social and audience editor, serving as their U.S. head of audience engagement. Before that, he worked as a reporter covering state politics in Washington, D.C. and the Twin Cities.


– Anna
